title: QRCC: Evaluating Large Quantum Circuits on Small Quantum Computers through Integrated Qubit Reuse and Circuit Cutting
problem: Quantum circuits that can be executed with high fidelity are limited by the small number and imperfect quality of physical qubits available in current quantum computers.
motivation: Quantum computing is an emerging computing paradigm but faces fundamental hardware constraints that limit the size and complexity of circuits that can be practically executed.
method: QRCC combines multiple techniques to run larger quantum circuits on smaller quantum computers. Wire cutting splits circuits into smaller pieces that each fit on available qubits, while qubit reuse runs different parts of the computation sequentially on the same physical qubits, reducing total hardware needs. The system also explores gate cutting, which breaks circuits at individual gates rather than at wires and is particularly effective for calculating expectation values—the predicted measurement outcomes of quantum states.
key_novelty: QRCC's key contribution is showing that combining qubit reuse and circuit cutting outperforms either technique in isolation, with gate cutting emerging as especially effective for expectation value calculations.
contributions: Integrated framework combining qubit reuse and circuit cutting
Comprehensive evaluation of gate cutting strategy for expectation value circuits
QRCC system demonstrating superior results over individual optimization techniques
Framework for evaluating large quantum circuits on limited quantum hardware

metrics.other: Fidelity, circuit depth, qubit utilization efficiency
